subject: Prospective PhD applicant (Fall 2027): user control and personal data in AI systems
body:
Dear Professor Li,

I'm applying to the Khoury HCI PhD program for Fall 2027. I'm writing to ask whether you expect to take new students.

I'm a product data analyst at Cadence, a fitness app. Last year I worked on the launch of AI Coach, a feature that changes people's workout plans based on their activity, sleep, and heart-rate data. I analyzed the launch test and coded the open-ended survey responses. Roughly one in ten respondents said something like "it changed my plan and I have no idea why," or asked how the app knew they'd slept badly. A couple had turned off health-data sharing. In the launch deck, all of it became "72% positive."

That's what I want to study: what people think is happening when an app uses their own data to make choices for them, and what would make them feel they still have a say.

Your COLM 2026 paper on autonomy and personalization in LLM agents is close to this. You found that risk-contingent autonomy improved users' perceived control, and that privacy concerns and trust held up better as a result. That's the kind of result I'd like to build on. AI Coach is much simpler than an LLM agent, but its users were asking similar questions: what does it know, why did it do that, and can I stop it?

I don't have publications. My research background is undergraduate HCI coursework (an interview study and a usability test) and four years of experiment analysis at Cadence. I'm happy to send my CV.

If you're recruiting for Fall 2027, I'd appreciate knowing. I'd be glad to talk briefly if you have time.

Best,
Riley Nakamura
riley.nakamura@example.com
